reason: Prioritize mixed3-4-g128: it has the lowest observed memory among recipes with nonzero quality near the target (1,925 MiB, 85%), so it is the most useful test of whether selective 4-bit protection can close the quality gap while saving memory. Second, test mlp3-rest4-g128 as an unmeasured hypothesis: protecting most modules at 4 bits may preserve quality while leaving MLP expansion weights at 3 bits. Neither is proven to meet both gates; no BF16 throughput reference or heldout results are supplied. The observed int4-g128 is the only recipe at 95% quality, but uses 2,299 MiB, so it is a fallback rather than a memory-reduction trial.
